neighbours.label: a bounded pause or holding interval inside a sequence of events: a timed break, pause, wait or stay ('a 10-minute ⟦break⟧ then…', 'a pause of ten ⟦seconds⟧', 'how long the pin ⟦stays⟧ high'). The − pole marks the gap 'between' events
fire: The class did twenty minutes of drills, followed by a five-minute break and then a short match.
There was a pause of several seconds on the line, and then the operator came back.
The timer records how long the door stays open after each delivery.
Knead the dough, give it a thirty-minute rest, then shape it into rolls.
The first half lasted an hour, followed by a twenty-minute interval and then the second half.
After the siren there is a delay of two seconds, and then the gates begin to close.
The script measures how long the signal stays low before the next pulse arrives.
The hikers climbed for two hours, took a ten-minute break, then went on to the summit.
quiet: The class did twenty minutes of drills, followed by a passing exercise and then a short match.
There was a crackle of static on the line, and then the operator came back.
The camera records who opens the door after each delivery.
Knead the dough, give it a dusting of flour, then shape it into rolls.
The first half was dull, followed by a lively second half and a penalty shoot-out.
After the siren there is a flash of orange light, and then the gates begin to close.
The script measures how strong the signal is before the next pulse arrives.
The hikers climbed the north ridge, took a few photographs, then went on to the summit.

notes: Probes were uneven: 'fifteen-minute break' 0.61, 'pause of ten seconds' 0.58, 'how long the button stays pressed' 0.78, but 'a short break after every two hours' 0.19 and 'rest for a few minutes' 0.13.
